newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey sells 60,000 T 96/97 sugar, to sell more.
newsitem.headline: Turkey sells 60,000 T 96/97 sugar, to sell more.

text.p: Turkey's state-run sugar refineries company Turkseker has so far exported 60,000 tonnes of white sugar from its 1996/97 production and will sell 40,000 tonnes more, Industry Minister Yalim Erez said on Wednesday.
"Turkseker produced 1.494 million tonnes of sugar in 1996/97...and was commissioned to export 100,000 tonnes," Erez said in a statement.
"It has so far exported 60,000 tonnes and will continue export deals to complete its commissioned amount," he said.
He did not specify the destinations of the sugar sales.

"...Turkey will not need sugar imports this year or the next. It has turned to a net sugar exporter from the position of an importing country," Erez said, referring to Turkey's imports in 1994/95 and 1995/96.
Turkseker, which operates 25 of the 28 sugar plants in Turkey, sold 50,000 tonnes in a tender in January.
Turkseker officials said earlier the company was planning to sell some 200,000 tonnes in calendar 1997 from 1996/97 output as well as using its stocks of an estimated one million tonnes.
Erez said the ministry had completed its payments to farmers for Turkseker's beet purchases.
Total payments were 54.5 trillion lira for 11.4 million tonnes of sugar beet, or an average of 4,775 lira per kilo of beet, he said.
Turkseker was aided by a 18-trillion lira soft loan from the government for its payments, he said.
Turkey's total sugar output for 1997/98 including that from three private refineries is expected to rise to 2.05 million tonnes from 1.85 million tonnes in 1996/97.
